To answer this question, we need to compare the average annual working hours of Canadians and Mexicans.

According to data from the OECD and other labor statistics sources, Mexico typically has one of the highest average annual working hours among OECD countries, often exceeding 2,000 hours per year. Canada, on the other hand, generally has lower average annual working hours, often around 1,700 to 1,800 hours per year.

This means that Canadians work fewer hours on average than Mexicans.

Therefore, the correct answer is that Canadians work less hours than Mexicans.
